citations.field: 人 entry; printed p. 698; PDF p. 711
citations.text: The 人 entry identifies the graph as pictographic, resembling a person in side view, and gives its basic sense as ‘person.’ It describes two early graphic variants—one joining head-like and torso-like parts, another joining head-like and arm-like parts—as equivalent in meaning; it says the former underlies the Shuowen Small Seal form, while the latter was more common in clerical script and developed into regular 人. The attached scan visibly shows the 人 headword, the form sequence, and this explanation. The continuation on PDF p. 712 is the separate 仁 entry, not a continuation of 人.
